name: classical-music-composers

description.en: 83 famous works of Western classical music composed before 1950 – operas, ballets and concert works chosen by how many Wikimedia sites (mostly language editions of Wikipedia) have a page on them. Front: the work's title in English and Swedish (where a title has been used for several works, the best-known one is meant); back: its composer. Titles and composers from Wikidata, checked against the Library of Congress name authorities and IMSLP.
description.sv: 83 berömda verk ur den västerländska klassiska musiken, komponerade före 1950 – operor, baletter och konsertverk utvalda efter hur många Wikimedia-webbplatser (främst språkversioner av Wikipedia) som har en sida om dem. Framsida: verkets titel på engelska och svenska (har flera verk samma titel avses det mest kända); baksida: tonsättaren. Titlar och tonsättare från Wikidata, kontrollerade mot Library of Congress namnauktoriteter och IMSLP.

method: Who did the work: the research, drafting and cross-checking were done by AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic) at Anton Wiklund's direction, with independent AI reviewers (factual accuracy, language, licensing and documentation, and a final re-check; see Quality control) and machine checks (the builder's Wikidata checks and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators). The cards have not yet been reviewed by a human subject expert.

Candidates (Wikidata, 2026-10-04): every Wikidata item with a composer statement (P86) and at least 25 sitelinks, from the Wikidata Query Service (query 1). wikibase:sitelinks counts the item's pages on every Wikimedia project: mostly the language editions of Wikipedia, but also Wikiquote, Wikisource, Wikinews and Commons; the whole selection ranks by this count, not by Wikipedia articles alone. This returned 9,616 rows for 8,262 items, most of them films, TV series and anthems.

Details: for the 8,262 items, in batches of 300, the English and Swedish labels, the composer and the composer's English label and date of death, the item's classes (P31) and the earliest inception (P571), publication date (P577) and date of first performance (P1191) (query 2).

Filter (a Python script over the saved results): a work was kept when its earliest P571/P577/P1191 date is before 1950 — or, with none of those dates, when every composer died before 1950 — and when its classes include musical work/composition (Q105543609), dramatico-musical work (Q58483083), ballet (Q58483088), passion (Q781815) or one of the other music classes listed in the filter under Queries, but none of film, animated film, short film, TV series, animated series or national anthem. The remaining works were ranked by sitelink count (all Wikimedia projects).

Editorial screening of the ranked list from the top, by the criteria in Selection: songs, carols, hymns, chant, anthems, patriotic and military songs and marches, musicals and plays with music were set aside as not Western classical concert, opera or ballet repertoire; numbered works without an established nickname (e.g. Beethoven's Symphony No. 9, Mozart's Requiem) were set aside as generic titles. Every work at or above the cut that was set aside is listed in Selection.

Title clashes: for the shortlisted works, query 3 found every other Wikidata item with a composer whose English or Swedish label is exactly the same as the work's label in that language. A work was dropped when a same-titled musical work by another composer has at least half as many sitelinks (this removed Verdi's Otello, 45 sitelinks, against Rossini's Otello with 26). Query 3 compared labels only, so after review (quality-control round 3) query 4 repeated the search with the titles actually on the card fronts, in each language, matched against the labels and the aliases of every item with a composer. Namesakes that are films, TV series, video games, theatre productions or popular songs were ignored. Every other namesake (an opera, operetta, musical, ballet or concert work by another composer) with at least 5 sitelinks is named in a back note that says which work is meant: Aida, Turandot, The Barber of Seville, La bohème, Manon Lescaut, Falstaff, Faust, Macbeth, Salome, Boléro, Pastoral Symphony, Orfeo ed Euridice and L'Orfeo. A few less-known namesakes are named too (Ferdinando Bertoni, Antonio Sartorio); the others with fewer than 5 sitelinks are not (e.g. Galuppi's and Federici's Idomeneo, Prokofiev's film music The Queen of Spades, Strauss II's quadrille Un ballo in maschera, Balfe's Falstaff). Works with a different title (e.g. Suppé's Pique Dame) are outside this check. Query 4 found no new clash under the drop rule: the only musical namesake with more than half a card's sitelinks, Massenet's Manon (29, against Manon Lescaut's 40), matched only through its Swedish alias 'Manon Lescaut'; its title is Manon, so the card stays and its back note names Massenet's opera. Every namesake named in a note is cited on the card with its Wikidata item and has a composer (P86) check.
The deck takes the eligible works in sitelink order down to 35 sitelinks, with the whole of the tie at 35, which gives 83 cards (the brief asked for about 80).

Titles: the English front is Wikidata's English label, or an English alias where the label is a generic numbered title (Moonlight Sonata, Pastoral Symphony, Sonata Pathétique, Jupiter Symphony, Canon in D); 'Eroica Symphony' is our own English form of the alias 'Eroica'. La traviata has no English or Swedish label in Wikidata, only a multilingual ('mul') label 'La traviata'; the builder's label checks accept a mul label. The Swedish front is Wikidata's Swedish label or alias, except where that is missing or would mislead; then the title of the Swedish Wikipedia article (a sitelink in Wikidata) or a Swedish form checked in Swedish Wikipedia's text was used: La traviata, La bohème, Symphonie fantastique, Spader dam, Sonata Pathétique, Jupitersymfonin, L'Orfeo (Swedish Wikipedia's redirect title for Monteverdi's opera, whose article opens 'Orfeo (italienska: L'Orfeo …)'; Wikidata's Swedish label 'Orfeus' is also the name of the mythical singer, and the bare 'Orfeo' is Wikidata's Swedish label of Luigi Rossi's opera) and Uvertyren 1812 (Wikidata's Swedish label is just '1812', which would read as a year; its Swedish alias 'Ouvertyren 1812', used at first, was not found in Swedish Wikipedia's text, which has 'Uvertyren 1812'). Swedish Wikipedia's text was read for those cards and for the Swedish titles that differ from the original-language title in a way a Swedish reader might question (Nebukadnessar, Ragnarök, Valkyrian, Rhenguldet, Läderlappen, Trubaduren, Eroica, Pastoralsymfonin, Månskenssonaten, Kanon i D, Törnrosa, Wilhelm Tell). Titles are tagged with the language in whose usage they are the established title, even when the title itself is in the original language (German, Italian, Latin or French): e.g. 'Der Ring des Nibelungen'@en, 'Das wohltemperierte Klavier'@sv, 'Così fan tutte'@en and @sv; Wikidata's English and Swedish labels follow the same practice.

Composers: the back is the composer from Wikidata P86 (every selected work has exactly one). The name is Wikidata's English label (one exception: for Gluck, the back uses 'Christoph Willibald Gluck', an English alias, the Swedish label and the title of the English and Swedish Wikipedia articles, rather than the English label 'Christoph Willibald von Gluck'); where Wikidata's Swedish label spells the name differently (transliterated Russian names, Handel/Händel, Rossini's Gioachino/Gioacchino, Leoncavallo's Ruggero/Ruggiero, the Strausses' II/I against d.y./d.ä.) the back gives the English and the Swedish form, tagged; otherwise the name is untagged.

Cross-check: for each work, its Library of Congress authority id (Wikidata P244) was looked up and the LC record fetched from id.loc.gov (…/authorities/names/<id>.madsrdf.json); the LC authorized heading begins with the composer's name and dates. For the 12 works with no usable LC heading (no P244, or for Giselle a heading without the composer) the IMSLP work page was found through the IMSLP API; IMSLP page titles end with the composer's name; the title cited is the one the page shows after any redirect. Every card's composer agreed with its second source.

Machine checks: every card has Wikidata checks run by the builder: the composer (P86), the English and Swedish front titles as a label or alias where they are one, and the composer's name as a label in each language used. Label checks were left out only where the card's title is not a Wikidata label or alias, as listed in quality control.

Back notes were written by us from the evidence listed on each card: Wikidata namesake items (each with a composer check), Library of Congress headings showing a work as part of a larger one, and Swedish Wikipedia for the Swedish title of a larger work (Triptyken). IMSLP page lists and English Wikipedia only confirm what Wikidata gives.

Dates in the evidence: each Wikidata entry gives the work's earliest inception (P571), publication (P577) or first performance (P1191) at year precision or finer. Sixteen works also have a coarser value, a publication date of 1850 with century precision ('19th century'); the evidence says so, since Wikidata does not date them 1850 (quality-control round 3). Four works have none of these dates in Wikidata and passed the filter only through its fallback, the composer's death before 1950: canon-in-d (Pachelbel, died 1706), goldberg-variations and brandenburg-concertos (Bach, died 1750) and nessun-dorma (Puccini, died 1924); their evidence says this instead of giving a work date (quality-control round 5). Alias lists in the evidence are the aliases seen at retrieval and are given as 'aliases include', since Wikidata's alias lists change. No date is shown on a card.
selection: Included: the 83 highest-ranked works by Wikidata sitelink count (pages on all Wikimedia projects, mostly Wikipedias; Wikidata, 2026-10-04) among musical works with a single named composer, dated (inception, publication or first performance) before 1950, that belong to the Western classical opera, ballet, concert or church-music repertoire and have a title that identifies them on its own. The cut is at 35 sitelinks, with the whole tie at 35. Because the count includes Wikiquote, Wikisource, Wikinews and Commons, 11 of the 83 works have fewer than 35 Wikipedia articles (Sonata Pathétique has 32 of its 35 sitelinks on Wikipedias); a ranking by Wikipedia articles alone would give a slightly different list. Excluded: every work that passed the filter with at least 35 sitelinks but is not in the deck, all 30 of them (Wikidata item, sitelinks): songs, carols, hymns and chant — The Internationale (Q49617, 133), Stille Nacht (Q172152, 79), Auld Lang Syne (Q211939, 55), Happy Birthday to You (Q167545, 53), 'O Sole Mio (Q205891, 50), Jingle Bells (Q406845, 48), Hava Nagila (Q131718, 47), Salve Regina (Q301934, 45), Waltzing Matilda (Q752873, 40), La Espero (Q141005, 38), Greensleeves (Q674738, 37), Bogurodzica (Q890692, 37); national, patriotic and military songs and marches — Katyusha (Q18288, 58), Rule, Britannia! (Q215729, 40), Farewell of Slavianka (Q331969, 39), Erika (Q700867, 37), The Sacred War (Q714119, 37); popular songs — Bésame Mucho (Q391180, 45), Gloomy Sunday (Q747869, 42), Over the Rainbow (Q161402, 40), You'll Never Walk Alone (Q728692, 38), White Christmas (Q1131761, 37), Lili Marleen (Q154968, 37); a play with music — The Threepenny Opera (Q212495, 46); generic numbered titles without an established nickname in both languages — Beethoven's Symphony No. 9 (Q11989, 65), Symphony No. 5 (Q188709, 56) and Symphony No. 1 (Q163493, 35), Mozart's Symphony No. 40 (Q231390, 35) and Mozart's Requiem (Q207875, 51; a generic title, and Wikidata also names Franz Xaver Süssmayr as its composer); and Verdi's Otello (Q172324, 45), whose title is shared with Rossini's Otello. The Radetzky March is kept as an orchestral concert piece by Johann Strauss I, though it is a march; this is a judgement call. Arias and parts with their own Wikidata item and rank (Nessun dorma; the four operas of the Ring) are kept as works in their own right. Sitelink counts change over time, so a re-run of the queries may give a slightly different list.

licensing: The deck is CC0 1.0. Everything in the cards — the choice of works, the titles, the composers and their names, and the namesakes named in back notes — comes from Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0, or is our own wording (the back notes, 'Eroica Symphony', and Swedish titles that are common names checked in Swedish Wikipedia, such as 'Jupitersymfonin', 'Uvertyren 1812' and 'Triptyken'). The selection is our own: a ranking by Wikidata's sitelink counts with the stated exclusions, not a list taken from any publication. The Library of Congress Name Authority File (a public-domain data set) and IMSLP (wiki pages CC BY-SA 4.0) were used only to confirm composers and namesakes, and Swedish and English Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) only to confirm titles and what kind of work a namesake is; no text or selection was copied from them, so their share-alike terms do not reach the deck. Facts such as who composed a work or what a work is called are not copyrightable.

rounds.lens: Machine checks against Wikidata, a second source for every composer, and the Swedish titles
rounds.summary: Every card's composer was confirmed by a Library of Congress heading or an IMSLP work page; no disagreement on who composed a work was found. The builder's Wikidata checks cover the composer (P86) of every card, the composer's name in each language used, and the front titles where they are a Wikidata label or alias. Title label checks were left out for: la-boheme (sv "La bohème"); eroica-symphony (en "Eroica Symphony"); symphonie-fantastique (sv "Symphonie fantastique"); the-queen-of-spades (sv "Spader dam"); sonata-pathetique (sv "Sonata Pathétique"); jupiter-symphony (sv "Jupitersymfonin"); l-orfeo (sv "L'Orfeo"); 1812-overture (sv "Uvertyren 1812"). Differences in name forms and titles between the sources are recorded below. (This list gives the final state after quality-control rounds 1 and 2, which changed the Swedish fronts of l-orfeo from 'Orfeo' to 'L'Orfeo' and of 1812-overture from 'Ouvertyren 1812' to 'Uvertyren 1812'; neither is a Wikidata Swedish label or alias; corrected in round 4.)

rounds.scope: All 83 cards: each composer checked against the opening of the work's English Wikipedia article and the reviewer's own knowledge; the builder's 408 Wikidata checks re-run; the selection compared with an independent query of works with 35 or more sitelinks.
rounds.summary: No wrong composer and no wrong back note. Two warnings: the Swedish front 'Orfeo' on l-orfeo was ambiguous (Gluck's opera, Luigi Rossi's Orfeo) and lacked a namesake note, and the deck described its ranking as Wikipedia coverage although wikibase:sitelinks counts all Wikimedia projects. Three suggestions: inconsistent namesake notes, a note for Vaughan Williams's Pastoral Symphony, and the Gluck name form. All were checked against Wikidata and Wikipedia and resolved; the namesake check was redone for the card fronts as used (query 4) with one rule for all notes.

findings.issue: The Swedish front 'Orfeo' does not point to one work: Gluck's Orfeo ed Euridice (in this deck) is often called just Orfeo, and 'Orfeo' is Wikidata's Swedish label of Luigi Rossi's opera (Q1118131). findings.issue: The description, method and selection said the works were chosen by how many Wikipedias cover them, but wikibase:sitelinks also counts Commons, Wikiquote, Wikisource and Wikinews.

The ranking was kept and the documentation corrected: description en 'chosen by how many Wikimedia sites (mostly language editions of Wikipedia) have a page on them', sv 'utvalda efter hur många Wikimedia-webbplatser (främst språkversioner av Wikipedia) som har en sida om dem'; method steps 2 and 4 and Selection say the count covers all Wikimedia projects and give the figures above.

findings.resolution: The namesake search was redone for the card fronts as used, labels and aliases (query 4), and one rule now applies to every card (method step 'Title clashes'): a back note names every musical namesake (opera, operetta, musical, ballet or concert work) by another composer with at least 5 sitelinks; films, TV, games, productions and popular songs are ignored. Under that rule notes were added or extended for falstaff (Elgar's symphonic study, 5 sitelinks, beside Salieri), aida (Elton John's musical, 19), bolero (Chopin's Boléro for piano, 9), salome (Antoine Mariotte's Salomé, 5), pastoral-symphony (Vaughan Williams, 10), manon-lescaut (Massenet's Manon, 29, which has the Swedish alias 'Manon Lescaut') and orfeo-ed-euridice (Haydn's L'anima del filosofo, 13, English alias 'Orfeo ed Euridice'), each with its Wikidata item and a composer check. No note for idomeneo: Galuppi's Idomeneo has 1 sitelink and Federici's 0. No note for the-queen-of-spades: Prokofiev's The Queen of Spades is film music with 2 sitelinks, and Suppé's operetta is titled Pique Dame, outside a same-title check. For salome the items the reviewer cited (Egisto Macchi, the Bizet item) are films, but query 4 found Mariotte's opera, now named.

(the Haydn clause comes from round 3's namesake check).

findings.issue: Query 3 matched only rdfs:label of the selected works, so fronts taken from aliases or our own forms were never checked for namesakes.

It found the clashes listed in round 1 (Rossi's Orfeo, Vaughan Williams's Pastoral Symphony, Chopin's Boléro, Mariotte's Salomé, Elton John's Aida, Elgar's Falstaff, Haydn's Orfeo ed Euridice, Massenet's Manon via a Swedish alias) and many films and songs; back notes now follow one documented rule (method step 'Title clashes'). findings.issue: Cards' Wikidata evidence said 'earliest date … 1850' where Wikidata has a century-precision value; the reviewer listed 18 cards.

Their locators and says now give the canonical pages: 'The Firebird (ballet), K010 (Stravinsky, Igor)', 'Symphonie fantastique, H 48 (Berlioz, Hector)' and 'Die Meistersinger von Nürnberg, WWV 96 (Wagner, Richard)'.
